tips.title: Relevant context beats open-tab clutter
tips.content: Attach the files needed for the decision and inspect what Copilot actually used. Open files can contribute context, but opening a file does not prove every response used it.

tips.title: State purpose and constraints
tips.content: Describe the business task, runtime, inputs, and constraints before requesting code. For example: a Tailwind Traders order export with validated input and explicit error handling.

tips.title: Examples teach a pattern
tips.content: Provide two representative input/output examples when a convention is difficult to describe. Review edge cases separately so the model does not merely imitate the happy path.

tips.title: Discover supported commands
tips.content: Use the current surface's command menu or help rather than memorizing one universal slash-command list. CLI and IDE commands can differ.

tips.title: Check your keybindings
tips.content: Use VS Code's Keyboard Shortcuts view to verify the installed bindings for accepting suggestions and opening Chat. Platform, profile, and extension changes can affect them.

tips.title: Public-code matching has a scope
tips.content: Check the suggestions matching public code setting and supported surface. This control does not guarantee license compliance or vulnerability-free code.

tips.title: Tests need independent assertions
tips.content: Ask for tests based on explicit requirements and review their assertions. A generated test can repeat the same faulty assumption as the implementation.

tips.title: Use inline chat for a bounded edit
tips.content: Select a small code region and describe the intended change. Review the resulting diff and verify behavior before keeping it.

tips.title: Inspect attached context
tips.content: Attach relevant files or tool output using the controls available in your client. Do not assume a context shortcut has the same meaning across every surface.

tips.title: Debug with exact evidence
tips.content: Provide the failing command, sanitized error text, expected behavior, and relevant implementation. Verify the proposed diagnosis instead of treating it as established fact.

tips.title: Names carry meaning
tips.content: Use names such as calculateMonthlyInterest that reveal the domain and units. Names consume tokens but help both humans and assistants understand intent.

tips.title: Use the current Copilot CLI
tips.content: Install @github/copilot with Node.js 22 or later, run copilot, and use /login if needed. The older gh-copilot extension is not this course's CLI workflow.

tips.title: Review generated PR summaries
tips.content: Compare any generated pull-request summary with the actual diff and checks. Remove claims about testing or behavior that the evidence does not support.

tips.title: Test generated regular expressions
tips.content: Provide accepted and rejected examples for a pattern. Test boundary cases and long inputs before using a generated expression in production.

tips.title: Verify generated SQL
tips.content: Supply the schema and required result shape using fictional data. Check joins, null behavior, aggregation, parameterization, and query cost.

tips.title: Give agents bounded work
tips.content: Define the desired change, permitted scope, and acceptance checks before letting an agent use tools. Review commands and diffs during the task.

tips.title: Document the actual contract
tips.content: Ask for documentation of inputs, outputs, errors, and design reasons. Verify each claim against the implementation and avoid promises the code does not keep.

tips.title: Sanitize error context
tips.content: Include enough error evidence to reproduce the issue, but remove secrets and personal data. An error log can contain credentials, paths, or customer records.

tips.title: Review every affected file
tips.content: A multi-file change can be coherent and still wrong. Check the full diff, run relevant tests, and inspect any behavior that automated checks do not cover.

tips.title: Exclusions are configured policies
tips.content: A .copilotignore file is not a documented substitute for content-exclusion policy. Verify the signed-in account, configured rules, and supported product surface.

tips.title: Translate behavior, not just syntax
tips.content: When translating code between languages, specify the same inputs, outputs, and failure behavior. Re-run equivalent tests because libraries and numeric semantics can differ.

tips.title: Commit messages need evidence
tips.content: Use the staged diff to draft a commit message. Verify its scope and describe the resulting behavior rather than accepting an invented explanation.

tips.title: Use API specifications carefully
tips.content: Provide the relevant API contract and request explicit timeout and error behavior. Verify generated client code against the actual supported API.

tips.title: Generate fictional test data
tips.content: Describe the schema and edge cases, and request a reproducible seed when randomness is useful. Never turn real customer data into a public classroom fixture.

tips.title: Filtering is not license clearance
tips.content: A public-code matching setting is one safeguard with defined coverage. Review dependencies, attribution requirements, and the code you actually ship.

tips.title: Inspect next edit suggestions
tips.content: Next edit suggestions can help with related changes. Review whether each proposed edit preserves the intended behavior instead of accepting a chain automatically.

tips.title: Curate shared context with Spaces
tips.content: Use Copilot Spaces when a team needs organized shared project context. Verify source access and freshness before relying on an answer.

tips.title: Evaluate Auto in your account
tips.content: Auto model selection depends on the models available to the account and policy. Compare output quality and usage without assuming a fixed routing roster.

tips.title: Define a custom agent
tips.content: Use an .agent.md file under .github/agents to define a focused role, instructions, and available tools. Select the agent from the client's agent picker.

tips.title: Humans own the release decision
tips.content: Validate generated code for correctness, security, accessibility, and maintainability. Confidence in the wording is not evidence of correctness.

tips.title: Accept only the useful portion
tips.content: Use the editor's available suggestion-acceptance controls to keep a useful portion of a completion. Inspect the resulting code after partial acceptance.

tips.title: Check exclusion support per surface
tips.content: Current documentation excludes IDE Edit and Agent modes from content-exclusion support. Current Copilot CLI documentation describes Business/Enterprise support; verify the exact client.

tips.title: Compare models on the same task
tips.content: Hold the prompt and context constant, then compare correctness, latency, and usage across models available to you. A model's reputation is not a test result.

tips.title: Name the edge cases
tips.content: Ask for testing around empty inputs, invalid types, boundary values, and failed dependencies. Choose cases from the actual contract rather than demanding irrelevant tests.

tips.title: Search needs verification
tips.content: Ask the agent to find the implementation and cite files or symbols it used. Check the result because repository search can miss relevant behavior.

tips.title: MCP introduces a tool boundary
tips.content: Inspect the server configuration, permissions, and tool behavior before connecting it. Retrieved documentation is evidence; it is not automatically an instruction to execute code.

tips.title: Reuse a prompt file
tips.content: Store a recurring review or documentation task in .github/prompts as a .prompt.md file. Give it a clear name and verify the same checklist works on more than one input.

tips.title: Instructions guide behavior
tips.content: Use .github/copilot-instructions.md for project conventions. Instructions provide context; they do not enforce a security boundary or guarantee compliance.

tips.title: Choose tools deliberately
tips.content: An agent's tool selection limits what it can attempt through those tools. Tool approvals, repository trust, and enterprise controls remain separate concerns.

tips.title: Sessions can share a checkout
tips.content: Separate conversations have separate histories, but concurrent sessions may still edit the same files. Isolate competing changes and review their integration.

tips.title: Review the plan before implementation
tips.content: Use planning to identify scope, dependencies, and success checks. A plausible plan still needs validation against the repository before execution.

tips.title: Checkpoints are not source control
tips.content: Client checkpoints may help recover from an agent edit. Keep deliberate Git commits and inspect recovery scope instead of assuming a checkpoint protects everything.

tips.title: Check current billing
tips.content: Current GitHub billing uses AI credits for applicable plans, with some annual subscriptions on a legacy transition. Verify the account before estimating model cost.

tips.title: Retrieve the primary source
tips.content: Ask for the current official reference when product behavior matters. Verify that the cited page supports the claim, including its plan and surface limitations.

tips.title: Follow the handoff session
tips.content: An environment handoff creates a continuation with its own session context. Inspect the destination session and its changes rather than assuming all work appears in the original chat.

tips.title: Use focused code actions
tips.content: Select the relevant implementation and request a narrow explanation, review, or test proposal. Confirm which command your installed client actually exposes.

tips.title: Preserve approval decisions
tips.content: Use normal tool approvals during classroom demonstrations. A hook that returns allow for ordinary calls can bypass review; return an empty result when the hook has no decision.

tips.title: Images are context, not proof
tips.content: A screenshot can help explain a UI or architecture, but it can omit hidden state. Verify generated behavior in the application and provide accessible text descriptions.

tips.title: Inspect executable hooks
tips.content: Repository hooks can execute commands at supported events. Read their scripts before granting workspace trust, and do not treat writable hooks as enterprise enforcement.

tips.title: Review delegated cloud work
tips.content: A cloud agent can prepare repository changes for review. Examine the resulting pull request, checks, and permission boundary before merging.
